Football.title: Ben White handed first England start in four years while Nico O’Reilly gets World Cup audition
Football.content:
Ben White handed first England start in four years while Nico O’Reilly gets World Cup audition

Thomas Tuchel has named Ben White in his England starting XI against Japan, talkSPORT understands.

The Arsenal defender was booed when he came off the bench in the 1-1 draw with Uruguay on Friday night, and even when he scored.

2 White scored for England against Uruguay but then gave away a penalty which saw them earn a draw in the Wembley friendly Credit: Getty

White received a surprise call-up to the squad having not played for England since controversially leaving their 2022 World Cup squad.



Despite the negative response, head coach Tuchel has handed him a start at right-back against Japan - which is live on talkSPORT on Tuesday night.

The 28-year-old will appear in the Three Lions starting XI for the first time since March 2022.

Tuchel's decision will give White huge confidence in making his squad for the World Cup this summer.

Manchester City starlet Nico O'Reilly is also in the line-up in what will be his third England outing since making his senior debut in November.



Newcastle's Anthony Gordon also comes into Tuchel's team.

2 O'Reilly will get his chance to audition for a place on the plane having just helped beat White's Arsenal in the Carabao Cup final Credit: Getty

More to follow...

Football.title: Ex-Arsenal captain tipped for surprise Tottenham transfer in radical new-look XI under Roberto De Zerbi
Football.content:
Robert De Zerbi could stir things up massively at Tottenham and make Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang the star of his new-look team next season.

That is the bold view of European football expert Andy Brassell, who has tipped the Italian to go in all guns blazing in north London ahead of his imminent appointment.

7 Roberto De Zerbi will have some big calls to make over the coming weeks at Tottenham, and beyond Credit: Getty

De Zerbi is set to be confirmed as Igor Tudor's successor on a five-year deal with the immediate goal to stop Spurs from suffering a first relegation in 49 years.



It barely feels like 5 minutes since fans were speculating on how Thomas Frank would set up his team, as an exciting new era appeared to dawn at the start of the season.

However, a shocking turn of events now sees Spurs two managers further down the line, and in need of an instant fix from De Zerbi.

While his first job is to get the best out of his current set of players to avoid the drop, he will no doubt have huge plans to make his mark in north London next season.

And European football expert Brassell has tipped De Zerbi to do this in spectacular fashion, by suggesting a bold, new-look starting XI.



Goalkeeper and defence

Starting in goal, Brassell went for an immediate change, as he called on De Zerbi to swap Guglielmo Vicario for Marseille's Geronimo Rulli.

The Argentine goalkeeper joined the Ligue 1 side alongside De Zerbi in 2024, and has been a mainstay between the sticks.



Stating his case, Brassell said: “Geronimo Rulli in goal. He's a terrific goalkeeper. He’s brilliant with his feet as well, so he's the best of both worlds.

“Okay, he's experienced - he's 33 years old now, but he's got plenty in the tank."



With Vicario facing criticism for his ball-playing abilities, and shakiness at times defending his six-yard area, Brassell insisted Rulli would be an all-round upgrade on the Italian.

7 Marseille goalkeeper Geronomi Rulli counts Ajax, Villareal and Real Sociedad among his former teams Credit: AFP

7 Luka Vuskovic is yet to make a competitive appearance for Tottenham, after being loaned out following his arrival last summer Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

He added: "I think he'll command his box better and he's way better with his feet, as well as in my view being a better shot stopper than Vicario.”

Moving into defence, Brassell tipped De Zerbi stick to his preferred 4-2-3-1 formation, and to keep their of Tottenham's regular starters in their backline.



Full-backs Destiny Udogie and Pedro Porro were both named in the potential back four, as well as star centre-back Micky van de Ven.

But one man not keeping his shirt was captain Cristian Romero, who has appeared unhappy with the club this term, with Brassell insisting youngster Luka Vuskovic could step in to take his place under De Zerbi.

Currently on loan at Hamburg, 19-year-old has impressed with his defensive displays in the Bundesliga, also scoring five goals.

Midfield: Rabiot raid?

As for De Zerbi's midfield, Brassell once again called on the Italian to introduce a familiar face from his time at Marseille.

7 20-year-old Lucas Bergvall has been tipped to replace Cristian Romero as Spurs captain Credit: Getty



Opting for two holding midfielders, the former Brighton boss was told to name 20-year-old Lucas Bergvall, who Brassell labelled a 'future captain'.

And to get the best out of the promising young Swede, the European football specialist believes De Zerbi should bring in 2018 World Cup winner Adrien Rabiot.

Having starred for Paris Saint-Germain and Juventus before joining De Zerbi in Marseille, Rabiot is now enjoying a fine season at AC Milan, who he joined last summer.

Tipping him to adapt to the Premier League, Brassell said: “I go for Adrien Rabiot because I think there is someone who I think should have played in the Premier League by now anyway.

He added: “You look at the size of him, the physicality of him. He's developed into such a brilliant player over the last three or four years.



"He always had the talent, but now I think he knows who and what he is, and despite various little ups and downs, he's been great for Milan this season."

7 Adrien Rabiot has fired in five goals from midfield in Serie A this season Credit: Getty

Ahead of Bergvall and Rabiot, Brassell backed De Zerbi to make £51.8million summer arrival Xavi Simons the key man in a No.10 role, with a fit-again Dejan Kulusevski to his right.

A familiar foe?

Then came Brassell's most controversial call, as he claimed De Zerbi should turn to Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang in the left wing.

This would certainly ruffle a few feathers at Spurs, with Aubameyang starring for bitter rivals Arsenal for four years and captaining them to FA Cup glory and scoring twice as Chelsea were beaten in 2020.



The Gabon international fired in 92 goals for the Gunners between 2018 and 2022, before spending time under De Zerbi after joining Marseille for a second time last summer.

Now 37, Aubameyang has proven he still has a knack for goals, with eight Ligue 1 strikes this term, and Brassell insisted he could be a real asset to Spurs, albeit controversial.

Making his bold claim, he said: "Perhaps a little bit out there for some people, I'd go for Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang.

7 Aubameyang won the FA Cup with Arsenal, but left after falling out with Mikel Arteta and also later played for Chelsea Credit: AFP or licensors

7 Brassell believes De Zerbi should go all out with a bold starting XI in north London



“He's going to turn 37 in the summer, so it's a short-term signing. It would be for a good time rather than a long time.

"He has been so good since he's left the Premier League."

Brassell claimed Aubameyang's all-round game is better now than in his Arsenal heyday, and tipped him to star on the left for Spurs, with Richarlison continuing to lead the line.

He continued: “He was a player who would touch the ball like 10-15 times a game and just really defined himself by his pace and his goals.

"Now he's still got really good pace actually, not quite what it was when he was 29 obviously, but he's still quick enough.

“He's so unbelievably intelligent, he stretches the game by taking the ball down the flanks, he defends really tigerishly. He keeps himself incredibly fit. He scores and creates.



“You look at his assist numbers over the last couple of seasons and they're absolutely brilliant. For me, he would be a better version of what Randal Kolo Muani should have been for Tottenham."

Admitting this may well be the move that neither party want, Brassell still insisted Aubameyang would be a real coup.

He rounded off: “Even though there's the Arsenal connection and maybe for that reason Aubameyang wouldn't be open to it.

“But if we're talking money and affiliation no object I think he'd be a really terrific signing for them.”

Plenty of their rivals will expect to be competitive, but to do that, they will need to rely on their attacking players to do the business.

Igor Tudor was sacked earlier this week but it doesn't necessarily mean Tottenham are out of the woods, even with an exceptional replacement.

Tudor was brought in to help bridge the gap between relegation and their poor form prior to his appointment.

Roberto De Zerbi has been selected as their answer, but can he make an immediate impact in creating the great escape for Spurs and avoid possibly the biggest relegation shocks ever in the Premier League?

But Tottenham are now winless in the league since their 1-0 away win against Crystal Palace way back in December 28.

There's now no room for error as even in February relegation looked very unlikely, as the teams in the drop zone weren't performing well enough to threaten their points.

West Ham have improved while Tottenham keep dropping points and are now just one point ahead of the Hammers with seven games to go.

They've won just three points from their last ten games and even a new manager bounce still might not be enough.

Spurs now need to at least match their points in their remaining games and it could come down to who they both face next.

Spurs next eight Premier League games

Sunderland vs Tottenham - April 12

Tottenham vs Brighton - 18 April

Wolves vs Tottenham - 25 April

Aston Villa vs Tottenham - 2 May

Tottenham vs Leeds United - 9 May

Chelsea vs Tottenham - 17 May

Tottenham vs Everton - 24 May

On the other hand, West Ham have: Wolves, Palace, Everton, Brentford, Arsenal, Newcastle and Leeds United for the final day of the league.

That looks like a relatively tough run-in with only three more home games of the seven, including away games at Chelsea and Aston Villa who are both aiming for top five finishes.

Tottenham have a poor record against their London rivals, losing in each of their last five, only winning once in their last 13 in all competitions.

Their best chance is arguably against Wolves away from home in late April, but even then the bottom of the table side have won twice in their last three in a massive turnaround of form.

Football.title: Roberto De Zerbi told major tactical problem he faces at Tottenham
Football.content:
Roberto De Zerbi faces a huge tactical dilemma if he takes over as Tottenham head coach.

The Italian has an agreement in place to take over at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

4 Roberto De Zerbi is closing in on the Tottenham head coach role Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

De Zerbi, who left his role as Marseille boss in February, is keen on an immediate return to the dugout.



However, he knows he has a tall order to turn around Spurs’ fortunes with just seven games remaining to steer them clear of relegation.

The ex-Brighton boss will have plenty to contend with upon his arrival however one factor he must overcome is how to accommodate Xavi Simons and the soon-to-return James Maddison in his starting XI.

Signs of progress

Simons, a £52million signing from RB Leipzig last summer, has largely struggled in his first season in English football.

However, the Dutchman has recently shown signs of improvement and produced arguably his best display in a Tottenham shirt in the 3-2 win over Atletico Madrid earlier this month.



The 22-year-old operates best in a No.10 role but can play in wider areas.

That mirrors the attributes of Maddison who is yet to play a single minute this season after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament injury in a pre-season clash against Newcastle in July.



Maddison is expected to make his grand return on the final day of the season however by that time De Zerbi will no doubt have one eye on next season’s squad.

And according to European football expert Andy Brassell, that could spell trouble for either one of Simons or Maddison with only one capable of filling De Zerbi’s golden No.10 berth.



“De Zerbi will want to attack, He’ll want to be on the front foot. What he will need is his full-backs whether he’ll play a three or a four to be adventurous,” Brassell told talkSPORT.

4 The Italian faces the biggest managerial challenge of his career at Tottenham Credit: Getty

“He’s got that in Pedro Porro and [Destiny] Udogie. He will need a No.10 and for that reason I anticipate keenly the return of James Maddison.

“I’m really keen to see how ready he is when comes back because if we’re looking into next season, a fully fit Maddison and De Zerbi goes together really well.

“I think that would be a real match.”

Brassell continued: “It was really interesting when De Zerbi persuaded Arteta to bring Ethan Nwaneri to him (at Marseille) on loan for the rest of the season, the main idea was to use him as a No.10.



“Not exclusively, but that’s the guy he’s been looking for all season to open teams up.

“Maddison is the most cut out to play that role in the Tottenham squad. Then again, maybe it’s Xavi Simons? It’s two incredible options.

4 James Maddison is set to return to action in May after missing the entire season through injury Credit: Getty

4 Xavi Simons has sparked into life after a difficult start to his Tottenham career Credit: Getty

“It’s been a difficult season for Simons.

Two's a crowd

“Long term, whether it’s De Zerbi or anyone else, I don't think Maddison and Xavi Simons fit in the same team," Brassell added.



But he was unimpressed with how Igor Tudor used the Dutchman in recent games.

He said: “What we’ve seen of Xavi Simons particularly recently against Atletico, to me it’s mad that, whoever the coach is, Xavi plays the game he did against Atletico and then starts the next game on the bench and he’s asked to pull it out of the fire when they’re losing against Forest.”

Football.title: When is the FA Cup final? Date and kick-off time for 2025/26 Wembley showpiece
Football.content:
When is the FA Cup final? Date and kick-off time for 2025/26 Wembley showpiece

The 2025/26 FA Cup final is already on the horizon and the remaining teams will be setting their sights on a trip to Wembley.

Last year's final saw Crystal Palace win their first ever trophy with a 1-0 victory over Manchester City at Wembley.

2 The FA Cup was the Eagles' first major trophy in their 164-year history Credit: Getty

However, the Eagles will not be able to defend their title after suffering one the greatest FA Cup upsets ever, losing 2-1 to National League North side Macclesfield in the Third Round this season.

Nottingham Forest suffered a dramatic loss against championship side Wrexham, crashing out on penalties.

Tottenham and Manchester United also exited early but plenty of big guns are still in it.

As we head into the next stage of the cup competition, here's everything you need to know about this year's Wembley blockbuster...

When is the 2025/26 FA Cup final?

The 2026 FA Cup final will be held on Saturday, May 16.

It will be played at Wembley Stadium and while kick-off is yet to be confirmed, it is expected to be at 4:30pm.

The FA Cup final used to have a traditional 3pm kickoff time, complimented by a lot of build-up coverage as the fixture was one of the very few games shown on terrestrial television.

However, things changed last year as 4:30pm was a compromised time between the BBC and ITV due to them both streaming the fixture and suiting the broadcasters better.

It coincides with the Gameweek 37 in the Premier League, meaning the two finalist who are Wembley bound will have their fixtures rescheduled.

2 It's the only major accolade the Gunners have won in six years Credit: AP

FA Cup 2025/26 fixtures

Fifth Round

Wolves 1–3 Liverpool

Mansfield Town 1–2 Arsenal

Wrexham 2–4 Chelsea (AET)

Newcastle 1–3 Manchester City

Fulham 0–1 Southampton

Port Vale 1–0 Sunderland

Leeds United 3–0 Norwich City

West Ham United 2–2 Brentford (Pens 5-3)

Quater-finals

Saturday, April 4

Manchester City v Liverpool, 12:45 - talkSPORT EXCLUSIVE

Chelsea v Port Vale, 17:45 - talkSPORT

Southampton v Arsenal, 20:00 - talkSPORT

Sunday, April 5

West Ham v Leeds, 16:30 - talkSPORT

Semi-finals

To be played on April 25 and 26 at Wembley

Which team has the most FA Cup wins?

Arsenal dominate the most English FA Cup titles, winning the cup a record 14 times, with Manchester United just behind with one less.

The last time the most successful club in this cup competition won was in 2020 in a 2-1 victory over Chelsea - it was also Mikel Arteta's debut season as manager.

United, who have 13 FA Cups, beat their city rivals in the final two years ago.

After those two clubs, Liverpool, Chelsea and Tottenham follow and are joint with eight titles each.

Other multiple time winners include Man City and Aston Villa with seven, Newcastle and Blackburn Rovers securing six, plus some historic wins from Everton, West Brom and even Wanderers all on five.

Football.title: Roberto De Zerbi reaches agreement with Tottenham to become third best paid Premier League boss
Football.content:
Roberto De Zerbi reaches agreement with Tottenham to become third best paid Premier League boss

Tottenham have reached an agreement with Roberto De Zerbi to succeed Igor Tudor, talkSPORT understands.

On Sunday, Spurs parted ways with interim boss Tudor, who lasted just 43 days in charge at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

2 Igor Tudor's short stint as Tottenham boss makes his one of the shortest reigns

Adi Hutter was initially linked with the vacant Spurs role, but ruled himself out of the running on Sunday night.



And Spurs are now closing in on the appointment of De Zerbi, who has been out of work since leaving Marseille last month.

De Zerbi was initially reluctant to return to club management before the end of the season.

He was told on Sunday the key reason he should reject Spurs' approach by Italian journalist Daniele Fisichella on Trans Euro Express.

But the north London side found a breakthrough with the Italian on Monday, and reached an agreement with him on Tuesday, with De Zerbi now set to become the club's third manager of the season.



In the process, De Zerbi will become the third-best-paid manager in the Premier League behind Pep Guardiola and Mikel Arteta.

Arteta is currently paid in the region of £15million by Arsenal.

His contract does not include a relegation release clause - highlighting his commitment to the Spurs project - though it does include a pay cut clause if Tottenham go down.



De Zerbi is expected to keep Bruno Saltor on as part of his backroom staff after the ex-Brighton defender was assistant to Tudor.

talkSPORT verdict

Simon Jordan delivered his verdict on Spurs' impending appointment of De Zerbi on White & Jordan with Martin Keown on Monday morning.



2 De Zerbi has previously managed in the Premier League with Brighton Credit: AFP

And Jordan believes the only thing the Italian is good at is 'creating chaos and disruption'.

"De Zerbi is creative, yeah, he's good at creating chaos and disruption with people that he works for," Jordan began.

"But he's a capable manager and at the end of the day, you have to put the players into the conversation.

"The players go and execute the outcome. How can the players possibly, in any parallel universe, be excused from the outcome?"



De Zerbi's first game in charge at Spurs, should he be appointed, will be the trip to Sunderland in mid-April.

Tottenham then follow up their game at the Stadium of Light with the welcome of De Zerbi's former Premier League side, Brighton.

The relegation-threatened Premier League outfit then see out the campaign with games against Wolves, Aston Villa, Leeds, Chelsea and Everton.

Football.title: Romelu Lukaku facing disciplinary action for skipping training as Napoli release statement
Football.content:
Napoli are considering taking legal action against Romelu Lukaku after the striker failed to report for training.

Tensions have grown between Lukaku and the Serie A club after he spent the international break in Belgium while recovering from injury.

3 Lukaku joined Napoli from Chelsea in 2024 - helping the club win the Serie A title last season Credit: Getty

And that has left club officials frustrated with reports claiming there had been a significant fallout between the two parties.

Napoli release strong statement

A club statement released on Tuesday read: “SSC Napoli can confirm that Romelu Lukaku did not respond to today’s call to return to training.

“The club reserves the right to consider taking the appropriate disciplinary action.

"As well as to determine whether the player will continue to train with the team for an indefinite period.”

Rumours circulated that Lukaku had decided to receive treatment for his injury away from the club and without permission of Napoli’s medical team.

And that has angered the Serie A club, who were anticipating his return after he withdrew from the Belgium squad for this month’s internationals.

But the 32-year-old quickly poured cold water on suggestions he is looking for a way out of the club by confessing his commitment to the Napoli cause.

Lukaku's address to the fans

In his own statement geared towards the fans, Lukaku wrote: "This season has been very challenging for me, between the injury and personal loss.

“I know there has been a lot of noise over the last few days about my situation and it is important to clarify everything.

“The truth is that in recent weeks I didn’t feel well physically, I underwent some checks while I was in Belgium and it turned out there was inflammation and fluid in the iliopsoas muscle, near the scar tissue.

3 Romelu Lukaku is at the centre of a dispute with his club Napoli Credit: AFP

"It is the second problem I have had since I returned at the beginning of November. I chose to do the rehabilitation in Belgium so that I can be ready when called upon."

"I think most of you saw the interview I did in Verona. I could never turn my back on Napoli, never.

“There is nothing I would want more than to play and make my team win, but right now I have to make sure I am clinically 100%, because lately I wasn’t and this also weighed on me mentally."

Lukaku is expected to remain in Belgium for another two weeks while he works to regain his sharpness ahead of his return to Naples.

The striker admitted that his difficulties on the pitch has adversely impacted his psychological well-being and physical output.

"It has been a very intense year, but in the end I will make it and I will help Napoli and the national team reach their respective goals when I am called. That's all I want," he said.

3 Lukaku has netted 15 goals in 45 appearances for Napoli Credit: Getty

Napoli will hope the dispute will have a quick resolution and Lukaku can return to action as soon as possible.

The reigning Serie A champions remain in the running for the title despite sitting in third place – seven points adrift of leaders Inter.

Napoli have eight games remaining to close the gap starting with the visit of second-placed AC Milan after the internationals.

At the very least Antonio Conte’s side must ensure they secure Champions League qualification for next season with Lukaku’s inclusion likely to bolster their hopes.

News.title: Incredible video shows one-year-old ‘Jenga prodigy’ in action – leaving his stunned mother’s jaw on the floor
News.content:
THIS is the unbelievable moment a one-year-old Jenga prodigy leaves his adoring mother stunned.

Astonishing footage shows the young child delicately extracting a wooden brick from the wobbling tower.





His mother cannot believe her eyes as he repeats the trick again moments later.

Completely unfazed by the increasingly unstable structure, the baby successfully removes a third brick.

Returning for one final attempt, the infant takes a fourth and final piece.

Katherine Stevens said she was playing Jenga with her seven-year-old daughter Daisy, when her son decided to join in.



Daisy held the camera as her younger brother Cameron expertly pulled the blocks free.

She also managed to capture her mother’s gobsmacked expression as Cameron carelessly went brick for brick.

Stevens posted the video on TikTok afterwards, captioned: “Apparently I have a Jenga prodigy.”

The extraordinary footage has now been viewed more than 13 million times.



One user wrote: “More amazed by the mom’s facial expression than the standing tower.”

Another added: “LOL. The look on her face.”

This is not the first time a parent has been left stunned by their child’s immense talent.

In 2018, Megul Garg recorded the highest possible IQ score of 162 at just ten years old.

This result placed him in the top one per cent of people who have taken the test.



The so-called genius benchmark is set at 140, with Albert Einstein and Stephen Hawking only scoring 150.

Speaking to the Sun, the young genius said: “I was in tears when I got the results back.

“I had just wanted to see how good I am against people who are really smart – I’m really competitive.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Genius clearly runs in the family as his older brother, Dhruv, also scored the highest mark possible when he took the test.

Mum Divya said: “It’s always going to be hard work to always find them something that is going to be intellectually challenging.”

News.title: Trump slams ‘terrible’ Nato but he isn’t ready to leave alliance to deal with Hormuz chaos ‘just yet’ after blasting UK
News.content:
DONALD Trump has slammed “terrible” Nato after taking a fresh swipe at Britain – but the US president says he isn’t ready to give up on freeing the Strait of Hormuz yet.

It comes after Trump launched a fresh attack on the UK for keeping its hands clean of the ongoing war with Iran, despite a deepening fuel shortage crisis.





The president repeated his scathing criticism of Nato, branding the alliance “terrible” and reiterating his call for countries to join the war.

Washington has poured countless resources into the weeks-long mission to release the vital 24-mile waterway from the regime’s bloody claws, with oil prices shooting up with every day Tehran maintains a foothold.

Trump’s tirades would suggest that US forces may be imminently withdrawing from the Persian Gulf, with the president demanding allied spectators go in and get their own fuel.

But he today confirmed that American military assets would continue fighting to reopen the shipping lane and will not be pulled out of the mission entirely.

“At some point I will, not quite yet,” Trump told CBS.

“But countries have to come in and take care of it.

“Iran has been decimated, but they’re going to have to come in and do their own work.”



Trump claimed that despite Tehran continuing to fire at ships passing through the strait, there’s “no substantial threat” as the reeling regime’s military has been “decimated”.

“If they’re having a hard time getting oil, let them come and take it like they’re supposed to,” he said of the US’ allies.

“They didn’t want to give a hand to anybody. NATO is terrible, and they’re all terrible.

“So if they want oil, come up and grab it.

“It’s about time they did something for themselves.”



It comes after Trump blasted Nato allies as “cowards” for failing to help him unblock the strait.

Trump was non-committal about when US forces would be withdrawn, telling CBS: “It won’t be long, I would say we are two weeks ahead of schedule.”

“We’ve done our job. It’ll take them 10 years to rebuild.

“We’ve had total regime change. These are different people than anyone has ever heard of before, and frankly they’ve been more reasonable.”



The president had previously set a four to six week deadline for the war to be over, but it has already entered week five.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has proposed that a multi-national consortium take over the Strait of Hormuz once hostilities are over, according to The Telegraph.

At a meeting with G7 foreign leaders, Rubio stressed that there would be “no fees, and free circulation” after the intervention.

Trump, meanwhile, posted a video on Truth Social earlier today showing enormous 2,000lb bunker buster bombs tearing through an Iranian ammo depot as he looks to finish the job.



An enormous mushroom cloud is seen billowing into the sky as a devastating inferno takes hold of the ammunition factory in Isfahan, Iran‘s third-most populous city.

Isfahan has been the target of repeated strikes from US-Israeli forces over the monthlong conflict.

It is a strategic hub that holds the majority of Iran’s 60 per cent enriched uranium, military bases, and one of several underground “missile cities”.

The city is home to one of three uranium enrichment sites that were bombed by the US in the 12-day conflict between Iran and Israel last June.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A satellite capture taken just days before the blitz suggests Tehran rushed to hide a truckload of highly enriched uranium in an underground facility.



It is believed that much of the reeling regime’s missile arsenal is now entombed in subterranean bases as the mad mullahs seek to retain at least some of their military might.

News.title: Body of missing man, 18, is found two weeks after car carrying five teens crashed into river
News.content:
RIVER TRAGEDY Body of missing man, 18, is found two weeks after car carrying five teens crashed into river

THE body of a missing teenager has been found with police sadly pulling him from a river following a horror crash.

Declan Berry, 18, died after a “tragic collision” when the vehicle he was travelling in entered the River Nene near Wisbech in Cambridgeshire.



Police had been desperately searching for Declan’s body for two weeks after a shocking crash which tragically killed him and another passenger, 16-year-old Eden Bunn.



There were five teenage passengers in the car when it veered off the road and entered the river at Crab Marsh on Tuesday March 17.

Eden’s body was sadly recovered from the water the following day, but at the time Declan could not be found.

Two 16-year-old girls and one 18-year-old man managed to escape the vehicle and survived the crash.

Detective Inspector Craig Wheeler said: “Declan’s family have been notified, and I would ask that their privacy is respected during this horrendous time for them.



“Our investigation into this absolutely tragic collision continues and I would urge anyone with any information about the collision to contact me.”

Cambridgeshire Police again appealed for witnesses or dashcam footage from the collision to aid their enquiries.

Anyone with information is asked to quote incident 515 of March 17 and report it via the force website.

News.title: More UK troops deploying to Middle East as Iran delivers hitlist of companies it will attack including Google and Tesla
News.content:
MORE British boots are heading to the Middle East in a major show of force to help shield allies from Iranian aggression.

Defence Secretary John Healey confirmed the move as the UK ramps up its military presence to defend key partners from Tehran’s growing threat.





Fresh troops and cutting-edge missile systems are being deployed across the Gulf, with Britain stepping up to protect the skies from Iranian attacks.

Healey said “Britain’s best” will stand shoulder-to-shoulder with allies as tensions simmer in the region.

At the heart of the operation is the powerful Sky Sabre system, which will be sent to Saudi Arabia within days.



Made up of radar, control units and missile launchers, it can blast incoming aircraft and munitions out of the sky.

A Royal Artillery battery and specialist battle managers will run the kit, integrating it straight into the kingdom’s defences.

Meanwhile, British Typhoons have already clocked up more than 1,280 flying hours across the region, protecting airspace over Qatar, Bahrain, Jordan and the UAE.

On the ground, the UK’s Lightweight Multirole Launcher is now active in Bahrain, while Kuwait has been equipped with the Rapid Sentry missile system and the RAF’s Orcus counter-drone tech to detect Iran’s deadly Shahed drones early.



Healey said: “Iran’s aggressive attacks continue to threaten our allies and interests in the Middle East.

“That’s why the UK has been flying defensive missions since day one of this conflict to protect British interests and allies – and today we’re delivering further support by extending our UK jets in Qatar and deploying extra air defence teams and systems to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and Kuwait.

“I am proud of the courage and professionalism our armed forces have shown since the start of the war and my message to Gulf partners is: Britain’s best will help you defend your skies.”

The military build-up comes as Iran issued a terrifying warning that it will strike major Western companies it accuses of aiding “terrorist operations”.

In a statement on Telegram, Iran’s Revolutionary Guard declared: “The main institutions effective in terrorist operations will be our legitimate targets.”



The regime then listed a string of global giants – including Google, Tesla, Microsoft, Apple, Meta, Nvidia and Boeing – warning they could face destruction from Wednesday evening.

Employees were told to flee workplaces immediately, while civilians living nearby were urged to evacuate within a one kilometre radius.

News.title: Shocking moment hooded mob of youngsters storm through M&S sparking huge brawl as police forced to break up chaos
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a mob of youngsters stampede through a Marks and Spencer while three police officers try to stop them.

The footage shows teens brawling in the food hall in Clapham, South London, on Saturday leaving shoppers terrified.





More than 20 youths are seen shoving each other in the frozen food aisle while the police officers attempt to quell the chaos by gently breaking up the group.

Lots of the youths are hooded or wearing hats.

The cops have little impact and many more teens stand on the side watching or filming the ordeal.



One girl even appears to be crying but ignores the policeman who tries to assist her.

Eventually the riot disbands and the police officers usher the youngsters out the shop.

The mob were understood to be targeting several other shops in the area, reports the Daily Mail.

The video has since gone viral on social media and users have branded it an example of lawless London.



The caption described the brawl as a “flash M&S robbery”.

One comment read: “Every school holiday is like this in London now.”

Another added: “The exact reason everybody’s food shop is becoming more expensive.”

This follows other recent, brazen crimes across the capital.

Last month a group of machete-wielding thieves smashed the windows of a jewellers using a moped.



Terrified passers-by watched the four figures raid a Turkish gold shop in Golders Green and some even tried to stop the theft.

Shocking footage shows the men threatening pedestrians with a machete while a second passes jewellery to a man on the moped.

CCTV from inside the shop shows the man crashed the moped through the front door while a customer was being attended to.

The thieves then smash glass cabinets and grab fistfuls of jewellery.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

One brave member of the public charged at the group with a wooden broom.



The bikes then departed with shopping bags reportedly full of stolen goods.

News.title: Dramatic vid shows major explosion rock Russian fuel plant with acrid smoke filling sky & at least two dead & 72 wounded
News.content:
THIS is the moment a huge explosion ripped through one of Russia’s largest fuel plants, killing two and wounding at least 72 others.

The fiery blast at the Nizhnekamskneftekhim facility in Tatarstan was so powerful that it smashed windows in buildings five miles away.





Over 60 firefighters stormed the plant, desperately trying to contain the flames and rescue the workers inside, of which at least seven are missing.

“I thought the roof of the building was going to collapse on me,” said one worker.

Another onlooker described the scenes as “hell”, saying that “the walls are shaking — it’s terrifying, what is happening”.



Ash was raining down as the inferno spread across 16,000 square feet and thick plumes of smoke filled the sky.

“All the ambulances rushed there with sirens blaring…” said another eye-witness.

“There are definitely casualties, and probably quite a lot”.

The exact number of deaths and injuries are still unconfirmed, and scientists are also concerned about ecological damage from the acrid fumes which fill the air of a city with a population of a quarter of a million people.



“No threats to residents or the ecological situation have been recorded,” claimed mayor Radmir Belyaev.

According to company officials, the blast was caused by a “malfunction in the equipment”.

The explosion comes amidst a spate of intense strikes from Ukraine on Vladimir Putin’s oil, ravaging the Russian economy.

Kyiv’s attacks on oil and gas ports and refineries in the last week have significantly damaged Putin’s ability to rack in cash from his oil sales.

The greatest destruction has been unleashed on Russia’s Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga which exports millions of metric tonnes of oil.



This latest explosion also damages Russia’s war effort as the chemicals and rubber produced in the blasted Nizhnekamskneftekhim facility can no longer be used to fuel Putin’s war machine.

Volodymyr Zelensky said he is ready for a ceasefire however, proposing that the two nations stop attacking one another’s energy systems over Easter.

The Kremlin is skeptical of the idea, even though Russia’s Baltic Sea energy post has been repeatedly hit by Kyiv in recent days.



One Russian military expert warned that Russia is “doomed to defeat” with the rise of Western-backed drones raining down on the nation.

Putin’s nation is economically dwindling and struggling to counter the superior Western-backed economic power of Ukraine.

The Russian patriot said Putin must accept a “shameful defeat” or defeat Ukraine with a strategic offensive.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He admits that Ukrainian counterattacks to Russia have been “rather successful” and have prevented Russia from decisive retaliation.

Putin has also faced problems sending communications since Elon Musk’s company SpaceX has blocked Russian military access to satellite-based internet.

News.title: Betting giant William Hill closing 200 high street stores within weeks with staff facing axe after Labour’s tax hikes
News.content:
BETS OFF Betting giant William Hill closing 200 high street stores within weeks with staff facing axe after Labour’s tax hikes

BETTING giant William Hill is closing 200 high street stores within weeks due to the “significant tax increases” unleashed by Labour.

The bookmaker blamed the “cost pressures” of the last Budget for the decision that will trigger a round of staff layoffs.





Chancellor Rachel Reeves is doubling taxes on online gaming from 21 to 40 per cent, while online sports betting will increase from 15 to 25 per cent.

William Hill’s parent company Evoke said in a statement: “Following a thorough review and further to increased cost pressures on the regulated sector including significant tax increases announced by the Government in last year’s Autumn Budget, from May we are closing a number of shops that are no longer sustainable.

“We are offering our full support to our retail colleagues who are affected by these closures.

“These decisions are never taken lightly, however in the face of rising cost pressures we must take action to ensure we can continue to invest in our core retail estate, with the right shops, in the right locations.”



It is understood that William Hill staff were informed of the decision today, with up to 1,500 jobs likely to be hit.

The 200 stores earmarked for closure represent 15 per cent of the bookies’ 1,300 current stores.

The Sun’s Save Our Bets campaign has been warning of the impact on the industry of Labour’s squeeze on betting.

Following October’s Budget, Evoke chief executive Per Widerstrom criticised the Chancellor for her “highly damaging” tax rises.



He said at the time: “These proposals are ill-thought-through, counterproductive, and highly damaging. It is clear these changes will significantly harm businesses, employees, and customers.”

Betting bosses are also warning about draconian plans for financial checks on punters they fear will lead to a rise in black market gambling.

News.title: Trump shares wild video of his planned ‘presidential library’ skyscraper in his signature style – but no books in sight
News.content:
DONALD Trump has shared a wild new video of a design of a skyscraper presidential library.

The two-minute long video shared to Truth Social by President Donald Trump shows a skyscraper with the Trump name and a US flag at the top.





At the bottom, visitors are shown entering the building through a grand golden entrance.

A portrait of Trump on the side of the building is captioned with “Make America Proud Again.”

Text in the AI-generated video appears to be gibberish at times.

The interior has various aircraft on display, among other iconography referencing Trump’s time in office so far.

READ MORE IN NEWS NOT KIDDING Vid of Kid Rock saluting Apache choppers hovering by his home sparks Army probe



This includes a golden statue of Trump with his fist raised, in the same way as when an attempt was made on his life in July 2024.

It is not known if the video designed by architects Bermello Ajamil is a final plan.



“This landmark on the water in Miami, Florida will stand as a lasting testament to an amazing man, an amazing developer, and the greatest President our Nation has ever known,” said Eric Trump, sharing the video.

Eric Trump, head of the library’s foundation, previously announced that Miami Dade College would be the site of the library last year.

However, the plans were derailed when an activist sued and a judge temporarily blocked the sale of the land.

“The Trump Presidential Library will be one of the most magnificent buildings in the world and a living testament to the indelible impact President Trump has made on America and its people,” White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said.

News.title: UK drivers warned about seven key roads over Easter bank holidays with huge delays
News.content:
UK drivers warned about seven key roads over Easter bank holidays with huge delays

If you're heading out this Easter bank holiday weekend then you may want to bear in mind that the UK is expected to be bustling with traffic – here's how to avoid the worst of the delays

View 2 Images It's likely to be hectic on the roads during Easter bank holiday

The Easter Bank Holiday is anticipated to be amongst the busiest travel periods of the year, with traffic volumes expected to match the 19 million car journeys witnessed on UK roads over the holiday period last year.

‌



Popular tourist hotspots are set to experience particularly severe congestion, where touring caravans and packed roads can generate additional strain for motorists.

‌



To assist travellers hoping to escape the bank holiday traffic this weekend, Mike Thompson, Chief Operating Officer at Leasing Options, has provided his expert guidance on dodging the traffic at the UK's biggest congestion blackspots, and reaching your destination stress-free and punctually.

‌



There are seven locations in particular that you need to be mindful of. These experience notably hectic periods at peak times, and it may be preferable to determine if you can navigate around them.

View 2 Images A row of cars are stuck in a traffic jam on a town street (Image: Getty)

Transport for London (TfL) confirms that the A40 is completely closed in both directions at all times between the Westway roundabout and Marylebone Flyover since March 20 until late April, indicating that the closure will remain in effect throughout the Easter bank holiday.

‌



With hold-ups and alternative routes in operation, the local roads surrounding the A40 are predicted to be exceptionally congested. The most significant Scottish delay anticipated over the bank holiday weekend is on the A9 south of Blair Atholl.

Traffic Scotland confirms that from the evening of April 2 until the morning of April 15, the stretch from River Garry to Shierglas will have temporary traffic lights in operation at all times, alongside a 10mph convoy system overnight and a 30mph restriction outside working hours.

The A487 at Commins Coch near Aberystwyth, Wales, is amongst the longest-running improvement schemes currently underway in the country, with temporary traffic lights expected to remain in place until June 23, making it the most noteworthy set of Welsh roadworks to be aware of.

‌



National Highways confirms the A52 is currently operating as a 24/7 one-way system for eastbound traffic between Priory and QMC roundabouts, with additional overnight full closures on March 30 to April 1 and again from April 7 to 10. For those considering travelling through Nottingham city centre during this time, delays could prove lengthier than anticipated, reports the Express.

National Highways also warns that the A1 northbound between Barnsdale Bar and Ferrybridge will be shut overnight on Saturday, April 5, from 8pm to 6am, with signed diversions in place, causing holdups for anyone with bank holiday travel plans across the Yorkshire region.

TfL has confirmed that the entire Gallows Corner junction, encompassing both the roundabout and flyover, will remain shut until the end of April, with only emergency vehicles, black cabs, and TfL buses permitted through. Consequently, local roads are anticipated to experience lengthy queues and considerable delays.

‌



The A30 Rawridge Hill holdups represent the most pressing concern for the South West. National Highways has confirmed an eastbound lane closure round the clock until April 17, with two-way signals, and an overnight full closure Monday to Saturday, 8pm-6am, between Honiton and the A30/A303 junction from March 16 to April 17.

The simplest and most straightforward way to steer clear of traffic this bank holiday is to travel outside of peak hours. Mike said: "If you can, aim to travel before 11am or after 7pm. Midday through late afternoon is often when bank holiday leisure traffic stacks up most. Since traffic can build throughout the day, it is better to try to leave earlier in the morning."

It's also worth downloading live traffic apps ahead of your journey. Mike added: "Apps such as Waze and Google Maps are useful because they can reroute you around live congestion, collisions and sudden delays. They are especially handy on Easter weekends, when traffic can build quickly around holiday hotspots even if there is no full closure in place."

Article continues below

His third piece of advice is to have an alternative route prepared. Mike said: "If you are heading somewhere busy, it helps to know your main alternatives before you set off. Official traffic sites in Scotland and Wales both offer route planning and live disruption updates, which can help you decide whether to stick with your planned route or divert before you get stuck in a queue."

News.title: UK weather maps show England set for wall of snow as one county faces 17 inches
News.content:
UK weather maps show England set for wall of snow as one county faces 17 inches

A band of snow around 80 miles in length is set to fall across the north England threatening to bring up to 17 inches in one area

View 2 Images (Image: Getty)

Multiple areas across the UK are in the firing line for snow in just days, as weather maps reveal parts of one county could be buried under up to 17 inches.

‌



Large swathes of the country are forecast be hit by 6am on Saturday, April 11, with a wall of snow forecast to bring drifts in northern England before moving further north into Scotland, according to advanced weather maps by WXCharts. These regions are set to bear the brunt of the storm with parts of Wales and Northern Ireland also poised for flurries.

‌



Cumbria, especially the Lake district, and Durham are set to be among the worst hit areas with up to 17 inches settling on higher ground in the national park. Also expecting snow by the same date are Cheshire, Lancashire, Derbyshire, Staffordshire, Northumberland, Durham, Yorkshire, Cumberland and Westmorland.

‌



View 2 Images Large swathes of the UK could be buried early next month (Image: WX CHARTS)

Full Pink Moon to be visible in the UK this week - why this happens and how to see it READ MORE :

Monty Don shares March lawn care task that makes grass thicker and 'healthier' than ever READ MORE :

Lighter accumulations are expected elsewhere, with the Scottish Borders expecting up to three inches, while parts of Wales - including Gwynedd, Powys and Merthyr Tydfil - are set for just under an inch of snow.

‌



The forecast comes after the Met Office warned to expect "unsettled conditions" as we transition into the new month, with the "wettest and windiest" weather expected in the west and north of the UK. While the forecaster doesn't explicitly mention snow, it does warn of high pressure causing conditions to be "unsettled overall".

The agency's long-range forecast, from Saturday April 4 - Monday, April 13, reads: "It is increasingly likely that unsettled conditions will affect the UK over the Easter Holiday weekend, with the potential for strong winds and heavy rain at times. The wettest and windiest weather is more likely towards the west and north of the country.

"Beyond Easter, a broad northwest-southeast split is most likely, though the extent of high pressure into southern areas is unclear. That said, northern and western parts are more likely to remain rather unsettled overall, with further spells of wind and rain, and areas further southeast should see the best of the drier, clearer interludes.

Article continues below

"Temperatures probably fairly close to average overall, but occasional warmer spells are possible in the south."

News.title: Inside England's bin chaos as 79 councils miss deadline and expert issues warning
News.content:
Inside England's bin chaos as 79 councils miss deadline and expert issues warning

Households have been told to change the way they bin their household waste, as food is now collected seperately - but a number of councils missed the deadline causing chaos

View 2 Images Waste collectors missed the deadline as councils were unable to make changes in time (Image: Michael Nguyen/NurPhoto/REX/Shutterstock)

Households have been warned on how to avoid maggots and rotting food if councils miss bin collections.

‌



The new rules for weekly food collection has come into play meaning waste collectors had to collect food waste separately to other rubbish, but clearly councils aren't ready for the new service.

‌



While households could be fined £400 if they don't follow the latest update, A BBC investigation found that 79 councils in England didn't meet the deadline for March 31 collection.

‌



This meant households who were disposing of food waste in small caddy bins could be more susceptible to maggots and mould growing. Before these new rules came into place, it was found that around half of councils were not collecting food waste weekly, while some have had the collections in place for more than a decade.

Have you been affected? Email niamh.kirk@reachplc.com

Every household to receive letter about major change happening in England now READ MORE :

View 2 Images Rules around bins have changed in the UK (Image: inyourArea)

‌



According to the BBC, councils had blamed this delay on the need for new specialist vehicles and funding issues, despite the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra) giving out more than £340m in grants.

Food waste when recycled properly can be used to make electricity, and reduces the amount of landfill waste and greenhouse gases. Also, by making these collections available to all homes may also help people reduce the amount of food waste in the first place.

Non-governmental climate action organisation Wrap called this new legislation "the biggest shake-up in recycling policy in England in 20 years."

‌



According to Defra's Simpler Recycling guidance, external waste collectors must collect the following separately from March 31:

Food and garden waste

Paper and card - although depending on where you live, this can be grouped with other dry recyclables

All other dry recyclable materials (glass, metal and plastic, including cartons)

Residual waste - this is the rubbish that cannot be recycled and so is sent to landfill or for energy recovery

However at least 57 councils told the BBC that they would miss the deadline aim to launch their service for all households by the end of 2026, including Darlington Borough Council, who informed residents this delay would be until June. While 31 councils had come to an agreement for a later start date.

‌



Ashley, a refuse worker in south-east England who frequently posts online under the name 'No1 Binman' said maggots and flies were attracted to food left in general waste bins as they tended to be collected less often. He recommended taking a food recycling bin out every week, and lining a food caddy meant food waste was less likely to get congealed and sticky.

"If you leave waste for a couple of days, it sticks to the bottom. Then you're the one having to scoop it out. Most councils allow you to use newspaper at the bottom of your food recycling." He noted that biodegradable bags could also help, and food recycling was for solids only, not for milk or sauces.

While Claire Shrewsbury, director of insights and innovation at Wrap told the BBC: "We're a nation of recyclers, but most households put two or more items in the rubbish each week that could be recycled - because of confusion.

Article continues below

"Food waste is where we'll see the big win. It's difficult to prevent all food waste and so recycling one kitchen caddy of unavoidable food waste could power your fridge for 18 hours, and a whole truck would keep that fridge cool for five years."

Have you been affected by the missed bin collections? Email me at niamhkirk@reachplc.com

News.title: Vicky McClure 'heartbroken' over grim murder as famous husband makes major promise
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Vicky McClure 'heartbroken' over grim murder as famous husband makes major promise

She is well known for playing tough and tenacious police characters in Line of Duty and Trigger Point. And now actress Vicky McClure is turning into a true crime TV sleuth

View 6 Images Vicky McClure and her husband Johnny Owen are fronting new Sky History show Britain's Murder Map (Image: .)

Line of Duty's Vicky McClure is fronting a new show delving into some of Britain’s most notorious historic killings. The 42-year-old’s partner in crime in Britain’s Murder Map is her real-life husband, Jonny Owen. Their Sky History show examines unsolved murders, miscarriages of justice and milestone cases that have changed the law, and the co-hosts speak to historians, police officers, victims’ families and a number of other contributors along the way.

‌



The subjects of the five episodes include the 19th century bodysnatchers Burke and Hare, John Christie’s murders at 10 Rillington Place, the 1959 murder of Antiguan Kelso Cochrane in London’s Notting Hill, which sparked racial tensions, and wife-poisoner Dr Hawley Crippen. Travelling the country together, Vicky and Jonny examine the crimes within their historical context and ask why they still resonate today – in some cases 200 years on.

‌



Jonny, 54, an actor, producer and writer, says: “Technology has evolved so quickly that it’s more difficult to be a criminal. You can get caught much more quickly now.” And while Jonny – who has a history degree – is keen to examine the history, Vicky says: “I’m just an ordinary person. I’m the viewer. I might have an extraordinary job, but at school I didn’t take to history, science, maths, all those kinds of things. It wasn’t me. I was always wanting to just perform.

‌



View 6 Images The Sky History show examines unsolved murders, miscarriages of justice and milestone cases that have changed the law, and the co-hosts speak to historians, police officers, victims’ families and a number of other contributors along the way. (Image: .)

“As an actor, you have to educate yourself on whatever it is you are playing. Therefore because of Line of Duty, I have done work with the real police outside of the show, and that made me interested in crime.” She adds: “I’m really nosy! I’m one of those really nosy people, I like to know everything. I like context. So for me, this was all about questioning whatever it was I was being told.”

The Kelso Cochrane case was particularly frustrating to examine. In May 1959 the 32-year-old carpenter was on his way home from a visit to Paddington General Hospital after injuring his thumb at work when he was stabbed to death in Notting Hill.

‌



At the time, witnesses saw a group of five or six white youths encircling Kelso, one jumping on his back. Two Jamaican men ran to help and took the victim to hospital, but he had been stabbed in the heart and died. No one has ever been charged with the crime. The Metropolitan Police says the file is not available to the public, as the case is still open.

View 6 Images Timothy Evans arriving at Paddington with two detectives. Timothy John Evans (20 November 1924 Ð 9 March 1950) was a Welshman who was hanged in the United Kingdom in 1950 for the murder of his infant daughter at 10 Rillington Place in London. Following serial killer John Christie's execution for the murder of his own wife, Evans was posthumously pardoned. The case played a large part in the abolition of capital punishment in Britain. (Image: Mirrorpix)

Of the closed file, Vicky says: “Well, something’s being hidden. Why would somebody redact, or hide or lock files away for a period of time? What’s really, really heartbreaking about that particular case [is] it feels like there was so much evidence.” But Jonny is more hopeful, saying: “The truth always comes out.”

‌



Take Rillington Place serial killer John Christie. When Welshman Timothy Evans’s wife and baby daughter were found murdered in 1949, lorry driver Evans – who was from Merthyr Tydfil like Jonny – confessed and was hanged. But he was wrongly convicted – his neighbour Christie was eventually outed as the genuine killer of those two and six other women as well.

Vicky says of Evans’s confession: “Some people say things because they feel forced into it, or even coerced. If you’re not privy to how the law works, or how it’s all going to unfold, it’s impossible for us to say why.” The actress was particularly moved by the murder of music hall performer Cora Crippen in 1910.

She was poisoned by her doctor husband, who dismembered her body, disposed of her limbs and head and buried her torso under the cellar floor of their London home. Vicky says: “Cora’s death was so twisted, and so psychologically harrowing.” As many of the historic murders involved women, the show has made Vicky question her own vulnerability.

‌



View 6 Images Vicky in the brilliant Trigger Point series (Image: ITV)

Talking about a daytime disco she and Jonny founded called Day Fever, she says: “One of the biggest things that I enjoy about it is I’m not worried when I walk home, because it’s eight o’clock at night, it’s not two o’clock in the morning. It’s not the safest place, the world, for a woman. You do walk around sort of conscious that, ‘Is that person following me? Do I need to put my keys in between my fingers?’ I’d be lying if I said I didn’t. I don’t have the physical strength to protect myself, and these women didn’t have the physical strength to protect themselves.”

Vicky is filming a seventh series of Line of Duty this spring in Belfast. The gritty role made her name – yet she says she didn’t seek out crime dramas and actually would be keen to mix things up, revealing: “I would love to do a comedy at some point, because I’m hilarious!”

‌



Appreciating her good fortune, she says of Trigger Point, in which she plays explosives officer Lana Washington: “The minute that was put on the table, I was interested, because it was something I knew nothing about. I was drawn to it. I like playing strong women. I think that’s because I come from a family of strong women. But yeah, I’d rather do crime than petticoats, put it that way!” Proudly from Nottingham, Vicky is keen to encourage trainees and working-class talent into acting.

6 View 6 Images Daily Mirror front page: Dr Crippen arrested (Image: Mirrorpix) 6 View 6 Images Kelso Cochrane, on the 18th May 1959 (Image: Collect Unknown)

Article continues below

She says: “TV production just keeps getting posher and posher. It’s still at an all-time low of 9% of people in the creative industries coming from working-class backgrounds.” She and Jonny run the Build Your Own Films production company to offer more opportunities. Vicky adds: “Line of Duty is a great example: Martin Compston, myself, Adrian Dunbar, we’re all from working-class backgrounds. We’ve all got accents that people can recognise, and we have those kinds of work ethics. I think that’s why people love Line Of Duty so much.”

And she has loved working on Britain’s Murder Map with Jonny – the couple married in 2023 after meeting in 2012 on the set of Svengali. She says: “When I’m working away we don’t really get to see each other, so it wasn’t bad to wake up together, travel together and just spend so much time together. It was a real treat.”

News.title: XL bully owner guilty after 'confused' pensioner mauled to death and 'eaten'
News.content:
An XL bully breeder has been found guilty after his dog mauled a pensioner to death.

John McColl died aged 84 after being attacked by Sean Garner’s "family pet" Toretto, who police had to shoot 10 times in order to bring under control.

It came after the seemingly "confused" OAP mistakenly entered the "irresponsible" owner’s driveway on his way home from the pub. Neighbours used a brush, a golf club and a spirit level as improvised weapons in an attempt to stave off the attack, but to no avail as the banned dog "guarded" the elderly victim "as if he were its prey or food". The court heard how the dog was found "eating" the pensioner.

Garner, of Dinaro Close in Belle Vale, was meanwhile said to have "made jokes" in Facebook voice notes while emergency services were fighting to save Mr McColl’s life, having earlier described the XL bully as "missing a few nuts and bolts".

Image: PA) PA)

The 31-year-old has been on trial at Liverpool Crown Court accused of causing his death by being the owner of a dangerously out of control dog in relation to the incident at his then home on Bardsley Avenue in Warrington, Liverpool Echo reports.

And Garner was unanimously found guilty of this single charge by a jury of eight men and four women this afternoon after two hours and 13 minutes of deliberations. The dad-of-three was heard to tell members of his family "love yous all" as he entered the dock prior to the verdict before - showing no reaction as he learned his fate.

Members of his family meanwhile gasped and burst into tears, with some seen with their heads in their hands. Garner will now be sentenced on April 17, and was remanded into custody until this date, with one woman telling him "love you Sean" as he was led to the cells.

Image: PA) PA)

Adjourning the case, Judge Brian Cummings KC told him: "Mr Garner, you have been found guilty on count one. You have previously pleaded guilty to three other offences. You will be sentenced by me in respect of all of those. That will take place on Friday the 17th of April.

"I am remanding you into custody. You will either appear via video link or be brought to court. Your sentence will be decided on that occasion. Any time you spend in custody on remand will count towards the sentence that you will receive. Plainly, that will be a substantial prison sentence."

Image: Cheshire Police / SWNS) Cheshire Police / SWNS)

The judge also excused the jury from serving again for the next 10 days due to the "nature of the evidence" being "certainly amongst the worst he has heard", adding: "Members of the jury, thank you for the careful attention that you have paid to this very serious and, plainly, very distressing case. I am extremely grateful to you all for the time that you have devoted to the case. My great gratitude to you all for your participation in this trial."

Turning to Mr McColl's family, some of whom were similarly seen to be in tears, Judge Cummings finally said: "My condolences to the family. I am very grateful to them all for their dignity and restraint throughout the trial."

News.title: Iran threatens 18 huge companies with 'destruction' – employees told 'stay away'
News.content:
Iran's most powerful armed force has branded 18 big companies "terrorist spy companies" and declared them "legitimate targets".

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said a number of American multinational companies in the technology and industrial sectors - including Google, Apple, Intel and Boeing - are "involved in terrorist operations", in a statement carried by Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency.

"We advise the employees of these institutions to immediately distance themselves from their workplaces to preserve their lives," the statement published on Tuesday afternoon said. "These companies should expect the destruction of their respective units in exchange for each terror act in Iran, starting from 8 PM Tehran time on Wednesday, April 1st."

Image: Google Maps) Google Maps)

Companies listed by IRGC

Cisco HP Intel Oracle Microsoft Apple Google Meta IBM Dell Palantir Nvidia JP Morgan Tesla General Electric Spire Solutions G42 (an Emirati artificial intelligence company) Boeing

On Monday, US President Donald Trump threatened widespread destruction of Iran’s energy resources and other vital infrastructure, including desalination plants, if a deal to end the war with Tehran is not reached "shortly". The threat included Iran's Kharg Island, which Trump suggested US troops could seize in an interview with the Financial Times published that same day.

Trump insisted on Monday that the US is negotiating with Iranian Parliamentary Speaker Mohammad-Bagher Qalibaf, but the former IRGC commander has denied that Iran is carrying out talks with the US. Qalibaf has said Pakistan-facilitated discussions were merely a cover for American troop deployments.

The US and Israel launched a new wave of strikes on Iran on Monday. Meanwhile, Tehran struck a key water and electrical plant in Kuwait, while Saudi Arabia and the UAE intercepted attacks by Iranian missiles.

More than 1,900 people in Iran have been killed in US-Israeli strikes, while over 1,200 people in Lebanon have been killed in Israeli strikes. Nineteen people in Israel and 13 US military members, as well as a number of civilians and soldiers on land and sea in the Gulf region, have also been killed in the ongoing war. Millions of people in Iran and Lebanon have been displaced.

News.title: Scott Mills dropped by Neuroblastoma UK charity as patron after Radio 2 sacking
News.content:
Scott Mills has been dropped as a patron by cancer charity Neuroblastoma UK. This comes after Mills was axed from BBC Radio 2 over the weekend.

Mills is no longer a patron for the charity, which aims to fund research into more effective treatments for children diagnosed with the cancer. His patron bio has vanished from Neuroblastoma UK's website.

A spokesperson told The Mirror: "Following his dismissal from the BBC, Neuroblastoma UK have taken the decision to part ways with Scott Mills, and he is no longer a Patron of our charity. We have communicated this decision to Scott and his team, and would like to thank him for his support to date. We remain unwavering in our mission to fund research to find better treatments, and a cure, for neuroblastoma."

Image: Dave Hogan/Hogan Media/Shutterstock) Dave Hogan/Hogan Media/Shutterstock)

The former BBC radio host first supported Neuroblastoma UK after a friend’s daughter was diagnosed with this aggressive cancer. Scott helped the charity to raise awareness of neuroblastoma and champion the work of Neuroblastoma UK to raise vital funds.

At the time, he said: “I’m really looking forward to working closely with Neuroblastoma UK to raise awareness of this cruel cancer and hopefully raise lots of money to help save more young lives.”

Mills was taken off air from BBC Radio 2 after his broadcast on 24 March and was replaced by Gary Davies. This was due to allegations concerning 'personal conduct', as announced days later. Now, the extent of the claims has emerged, with the Met Police investigating in 2016 over allegations of serious sexual offences which took place between 1997 and 2000.

The case was dropped at the time because of a lack of evidence. It's not known if the BBC were aware of the investigation at the time. A Met Police spokesperson told us on Monday: "In December 2016, the Met began an investigation following a referral from another police force. The investigation related to allegations of serious sexual offences against a teenage boy.

“These were reported to have taken place between 1997 and 2000. As part of these inquiries, a man who was in his 40s at the time of the interview, was questioned by police under caution in July 2018.

Image: CREDIT LINE:BBC/Owen Scurfield) CREDIT LINE:BBC/Owen Scurfield)

“A full file of evidence was submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service, who determined the evidential threshold had not been met to bring charges. Following this advice, the investigation was closed in May 2019."

Sources have said the BBC acted "quickly and decisively" last week following a complaint. Since Scott was fired, the license payer-funded corporation has remained in contact with the complainant. Mills has remained silent since the Mirror first reported that he had been fired. BBC staff said they were "shell-shocked" and there were "audible" gasps in the BBC studios when our story was published.

The BBC's director of Music, Lorna Clarke, sent an email to staff informing them that Mills would not be returning to work. She told staff: "I wanted to personally let you know that Scott Mills has left the Breakfast show, and the BBC. I know that this news will be sudden and unexpected, and therefore must come as a shock.

"Not least as so many of us have worked with Scott over a great many years, across a broad range of our programmes on R1, 5Live, R2 and TV. I felt it was important to share this news with you at the earliest opportunity.

"Of course, it will also come as a shock to our audience and loyal breakfast show listeners too. I will update everyone with more information on plans for the show when I’m able to. While I appreciate many of you will have questions, I hope you can understand that I am not going to be saying anything further now."

Meanwhile, the BBC said in a statement: "While we do not comment on matters relating to individuals, we can confirm Scott Mills is no longer contracted to work with the BBC."

News.title: 'Sweet' missing girl found dead at Owston Hall golf course is pictured
News.content:
The "sweet little girl" who drowned in a golf course pond has been named in heartbreaking tributes.

Nyla May Bradshaw, seven, was found in water at Owston Hall golf course in Doncaster on Monday morning following a huge search and rescue operation. In a tribute shared online, mum Hayley Beardsley wrote: "It breaks my heart to write this, but today we lost our beautiful daughter Nyla May Bradshaw at just seven years old.

"She was our whole world full of love, laughter, and the brightest smile that could light up any room. She brought so much joy into our lives and into the lives of everyone who knew her. Our sweet little girl will be loved forever and never, ever forgotten.

"Forever 7 my girl, this isn’t goodbye - it’s an until we meet again. You have family up there who will look after you. You were too special for this earth. Run as free as you want now, my gorgeous girl."

Image: Google) Google)

Family friend Charlotte said: "She was my best friend’s daughter – our beloved little girl. She was beautiful."

A fundraiser has been set up on GoFundMe to support the family with funeral costs. It describes Nyla as a "deeply loved little girl" and says she was autistic and non-verbal, adding that she drowned while she was "not in the care of her parents".

"Her family are now facing the unimaginable pain of losing their beautiful daughter, alongside many unanswered questions and the overwhelming responsibility of arranging her funeral," the fundraiser said.

Emergency services launched a large-scale search after Nyla was reported missing on Monday morning. Specialist resources, including drones and police aircraft, were deployed as officers worked to locate her.

A South Yorkshire Police spokesperson said: "Yesterday, Monday 30 March, officers responded to the death of a child in Doncaster. At 9.50am, a report was made that a child had gone missing in the Skellow area of the city. Officers and additional resources including police drones and the police aircraft were deployed.

“Following an extensive search, the child was located in a pond on Owston Hall golf course. Sadly, despite the best efforts of emergency services colleagues, they were pronounced deceased. The child's family has been informed and is being supported by our officers. The thoughts of everybody at SYP are with them at this devastating time."
